principios.texto: In my deep learning final project I trained four networks from scratch and compared them with paired significance tests. The simplest one won. At work I apply the same rule to forecasting: machine learning models compete for each brand and the best forecast wins. A bigger model is a hypothesis to test, not a default.

Repetitive work is where automation pays first. At work, reporting that took about 6 h per brand now takes 5 minutes for all of them, and I'm building it into a web panel for the whole department. On my own time the same idea became stepdub, which records what you do on screen and writes readable Python that does it again.
Since 2013 in aftersales: warranty analysis, fleet maintenance contracts, technical campaigns, and now parts and accessories. The code serves the operation, not the other way round.
